1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bb5 Nd4 5..strategy: Castles at once, putting the king away and a rook on f1 to guard f2, where the c5 bishop aims from behind its own d4 knight. White keeps the extra pawn for the moment and accepts a sharp game, since the d4 knight attacks the b5 bishop, which only the c3 knight covers.

Castles in turn and bets on activity against the pawn it is down: the d4 knight attacks the b5 bishop, the f6 knight presses on e4 and the c5 bishop lines up on f2. White's e5 knight stays, so Black has to make that piece activity count.
